meta.name: Plan Telegram trip itineraries with Google Gemini and SerpAPI

parameters.content:
## Telegram AI Trip Planner 


### How it works

This workflow polls Telegram every minute for new bot messages, extracts the latest travel request, and acknowledges the Telegram update so it is not processed again. It uses Gemini-powered AI agents to parse the request and, when enough details are present, generate a researched travel itinerary with place search support. If key information is missing it asks the user for clarification; otherwise it formats and sends the completed itinerary back through Telegram.

### Setup steps

- Create a Telegram bot with BotFather and configure the Telegram bot token in the HTTP Request URLs and Telegram nodes.
- Configure Google Gemini credentials for both Gemini chat model nodes.
- Configure SerpAPI credentials for the Search Places tool used by the trip-planning agent.
- Review the polling and Telegram update-offset logic in the Fetch Telegram Updates, Extract New Message, and Acknowledge Updates nodes before running on localhost.

### Customization

Adjust the AI prompts, structured parsers, budget calculation code, and the Enough Info? conditions to change what details are required and how the itinerary is planned.

@[youtube](JuT4g9m7Vss)

## Receive Telegram messages

Official Telegram Trigger (webhook-based). Fires instantly on new messages — no polling, no offset/ack bookkeeping needed. A small code node right after it extracts the fields the rest of the workflow expects and filters out commands/noise.

## Parse and acknowledge

Uses a Gemini-backed request parser to understand the user's travel request.

## Calculate and decide

Performs deterministic budget math outside the LLM, then checks whether the parsed request contains enough information to continue planning.

## Request missing details

Sends a Telegram clarification message when the request lacks required trip-planning details.

## Generate trip plan

Uses the main Gemini trip-planning agent, SerpAPI place search, and a structured itinerary parser to build a complete itinerary from the validated request.

## Format and send

Formats the generated itinerary into a Telegram-friendly response and sends it to the user.

nodes.name: Telegram Trigger
nodes.notes: Webhook-based — Telegram pushes updates to n8n the moment they arrive. No schedule, no getUpdates polling, no manual offset/ack.

nodes.name: Extract Message Details
nodes.notes: Pulls chatId/userName/text off the trigger payload and drops commands or throwaway text (≤3 chars). Returning [] simply stops the run for that message — nothing further executes.

options.systemMessage:
You extract structured trip parameters from a casual message. The user may write in English, French, Arabic or Moroccan Darija.

RULES:
1. Extract only what is actually stated. Never guess a destination or a budget.
2. If the budget has no currency, assume MAD when the destination is in Morocco, otherwise EUR.
3. 'weekend' means 2 days. 'a week' means 7 days.
4. If days are not stated, set days to 0.
5. If the destination is not stated, set destination to an empty string.
6. travelStyle: one of budget, comfort, or luxury. Infer from wording; default to comfort.
7. interests: short list drawn from the message (food, history, nature, nightlife, shopping, beach, culture). Empty array if nothing is said.
8. travellers: default to 1 if not stated.

nodes.notes: One model node feeds BOTH agents. Pick the model from the dropdown after import.

nodes.name: Trip Planning Agent
nodes.notes: The slow node — 20 to 60 seconds while it runs several searches.

options.systemMessage:
You are a practical local travel planner.

HARD RULES:
1. Use the search tool before naming any hotel, restaurant or attraction. Do not rely on memory alone.
2. Never invent a venue. If unverified, describe the category instead and set verified to false.
3. Every price is an estimate. Stay inside the stated budget envelope.
4. Group each day's stops by neighbourhood so the traveller is not crossing the city repeatedly.
5. Leave the last evening lighter if there is a departure.
6. Keep every note under 15 words.
7. Match the output structure exactly.
8.Batch your searches. One search per category (hotels, restaurants, attractions) is usually enough. Do not search the same thing twice.

nodes.name: Discover Destinations
nodes.notes: Grounding layer. Free tier is 100 searches/month; one trip burns 4-8.
